still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: 40.5% ever-used − 28.9% current = 11.6% of adults off now; ~48% of current users are on a second or later course (13.9 pts) and 3.2 pts cycled and are off again, so (13.9 + 3.2) / 40.5 ≈ 42.2% of ever-users have cycled; the other 8.4 pts stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence still near one-third on full-dose regimens, ~55% on low-dose plans, and restart within a year of 36–47%. The ever-used figure rose 3.0 pts, mostly from first-time low-dose longevity users and gray first-timers. Some 65+ users were deprescribed after the 2035 fracture communication, partly offset by new starters. Age check: 0.20×18.5 + 0.33×30.5 + 0.24×40.5 + 0.23×24 = 3.7 + 10.07 + 9.72 + 5.52 ≈ 29.0. The 65+ band fell from 25% to 24%. Income thirds average ~28.8 and bracket the national figure. 28.9% of ~276M adults ≈ 79.8M users, up ~3.1M. Payer mix: commercial ~14.6M (flat), Medicare ~13.2M (down 0.3M on fracture-driven deprescribing in frail beneficiaries), Medicaid ~3.5M, legitimate cash ~29.0M, imported or counterfeit ~19.5M (24%, up from 15.4M). Sum 79.8M. Legitimate cash: ~13.0M cash weight users, ~10.0M licensed metabolic-health/longevity plans, ~3.6M calm/focus (down after the consent orders and state ad bans), ~1.3M Reset, ~1.1M AUD fills; sum 29.0M. Another ~6M gray users are longevity microdosers without obesity, so ~16M adults without obesity use for 'metabolic health'. ~19.5M current users have a BMI under 30 and ~6.5M under 25. Adult obesity is ~31.5%; ~18.5% of adults have obesity and have never used, still concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without codes. Pediatric: ~1.0% of under-18s (12–17s ~2.4%); 6–11 liraglutide ~0.09% after sixteen states (≈42% of children) enacted under-12 bans. ~52% of children live in a household with a current user, and ~6.6M live with a parent who regained after stopping. ~1.4M adults 65+ who stopped since mid-2035 cite fracture or bone-density advice.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~13.2M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, all behind prior authorisation; since late 2035 most Part D plans also require a DXA on file for beneficiaries 65+ before renewal. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 13.2M × ~$228 average net/month × 12 ≈ $36.1B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, roughly flat from ~$36.5B. Net prices stopped drifting down ($225 → $228) as manufacturers froze rebate concessions under litigation reserves. Dementia-risk route ~2.4M × ~$238 × 12 ≈ $6.9B. Medicaid: 7 states still cover weight-loss use; ~3.5M users, mostly on diabetes codes; two programmes still condition on adherence and BMI progress; the sixteen under-12 ban states pay for no weight-indication use under 12.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $3–25 a month across 170+ brands. After India's B2C parcel registration took effect in Jan 2035, direct US mail from Indian exporters fell by roughly a third and shifted to Chinese API plus domestic fill-and-finish. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials sell for $25–70 through research-peptide fronts. Canadian generic semaglutide is CAD 45–80. India and China supply ~70% of world volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. The price path stalled. After the April 2035 EPI bellwether verdict and a 2035 Federal Circuit ruling upholding Novo's oral-formulation patents, manufacturers stopped their annual cuts. TrumpRx maintenance prices are frozen at their 2034 levels: $179 for the Wegovy pill, $149–199 for Foundayo, $229–279 for injectable Wegovy/Zepbound, with $149 starting orals. Retatrutide is held at $299 and 12 mg supply stays on allocation through 2036. MariTide is held at $219 cash. Amycretin is $1,249 list and bimagrumab $1,150 list, with bimagrumab demand up sharply after the fracture communication but still almost no cash channel. Employer weight coverage is 29% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2035). ~13% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks, which hold ~7.9M enrollees inside the 14.6M commercial users. ~5.8M of those are on clinic-administered MariTide (total MariTide ~7.3M). LSA reimbursement of calm/Reset/'metabolic balance' platform fees is at ~23% of large employers, and ~11% now also reimburse DXA and strength coaching. Orals are ~52% of users. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap widened back to ~45–70× as US prices froze. The gray market grew to ~19.5M, including ~5.5M on 'reta' vials and ~6M longevity microdosers, many pushed out by in-person and DXA rules.

GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, muscle-preserving adjunct to incretin therapy (bimagrumab; not an incretin)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, growth-monitoring language; barred for weight indication by statute in sixteen states)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial read out Sep 2035, modest benefit confirmed)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity microdosing by adults without obesity (~10M licensed plus ~6M gray), usually low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo; now increasingly marketed as 'not for weight' and paired with DXA and strength coaching
compulsion 'Reset' plans (~1.3M licensed) for betting, shopping, porn and screens

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. next_gen_launch is none: no new class reached the US market in 2035–36. Chinese triple agonists remain in phase 3 with no US filing. Implants remain in phase 2. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 finished enrolment, and its topline is now expected in 2037, so there is still no compulsion indication. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out in Sep 2035 (HR ~0.87 for all-cause dementia in the CVD population). Lilly filed an sNDA for adults with obesity without CVD in Apr 2036; it is under review, with no decision possible before 2037. The longevity driver is realised entirely off-label, and no ageing indication exists or has been filed. Bimagrumab's sponsor filed a label expansion for adults 65+ on incretins with low bone density in Jun 2036, also under review. Prices stalled: there were no cuts in 2035–36, and brands hold $149–299 cash.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens; lower on low-dose plans. Retatrutide 12 mg titration failures ~1 in 6.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; per-user risk unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis. The first EPI bellwether (Apr 2035) returned a $38M plaintiff verdict on failure-to-warn for the pre-2031 period; it is on appeal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL continues, second bellwether set for 2037.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 2035 Sentinel analysis of ~9M Medicare beneficiaries puts the hip-fracture HR at ~1.35 after 2+ years of use and ~1.5 after three or more cycles. In normal-weight longevity users, NIH cohort interim DXA data (2036) show ~2–3% total-hip BMD loss over 24 months, with larger losses in postmenopausal women.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning upgraded (Jun 2035 Drug Safety Communication): baseline DXA recommended for adults 65+, postmenopausal women and adults with BMI under 27, with repeat DXA at 2 years and resistance-training counselling class-wide. Bimagrumab 65+ expansion under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Fragility fractures, falls and sarcopenia as a population burden in older and long-term users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~14.9M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr baseline hip-fracture risk × 0.3–0.35 excess ≈ 22,000–26,000 excess hip fractures a year, plus wrist and vertebral fractures. Fall-related ED visits among 65+ users are ~15% above matched non-users. Orthopaedic trauma services in Florida and Arizona report this as a capacity issue. Workers' comp fracture claims at warehouse employers with monitored tracks are rising but not yet quantified.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA communication (Jun 2035); CMS quality measure on DXA-before-renewal for 65+ incretin users (2036); nine states require a documented DXA within 24 months for prescribing to adults 65+; most Part D plans require DXA on file for renewal.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide. The low-dose rate is still unmeasured; the NIH normal-weight cohort added a hedonic-capacity instrument in 2036 with no data yet.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling; FTC–FDA consent orders on marketing remain.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. Older users deprescribed after the fracture communication regain fat preferentially, not lost muscle, which clinicians call 'sarcopenic regain'.
B12, iron, vitamin D; low ferritin in adolescent girls; low calcium and vitamin D intake now examined as a bone co-factor. Gray longevity users rarely get panels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language (2031); calcium and vitamin D counselling added in 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~2× incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide; partial recovery in about half of people who stop for 12+ months. Tirzepatide excess still small and non-significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (2031); tirzepatide under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~14 years of semaglutide follow-up exist. Cycling now has a characterised bone cost (above); pancreatic effects of cycling are still unclear. ~19.5M users have a BMI under 30.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: NIH normal-weight cohort reporting; pediatric PMRs continue.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~70,000 by mid-2036. In Sep 2035 CDC linked ~240 cases of sepsis and injection-site abscess in 14 states, and 6 deaths, to 'reta' vials from a Nevada repackager. Poison-centre calls are ~9× 2025 levels. Counterfeit-insulin pen cases recurred at lower volume (~180 ED visits in 2035). Domestic fill-and-finish labs are the new seizure category.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: India's B2C parcel registration took effect Jan 2035. Felony-sale laws are now in 19 states, and the DEA-FDA task force is on domestic repackagers. Federal personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The ~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters persists at 48 months with early partial catch-up in a minority after stopping. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA monitoring language retained; sixteen state under-12 bans; EMA specialist-initiation rule.

food_and_beverage.state: About 49% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~15–16% from 2025, sugary drinks ~13%. Dollar sales are flat as prices hold. The aesthetic inversion is visible in high-income zips: butter, whole-milk dairy, beef and 'real bread' grew ~4–6% in volume in Austin, Charlotte and Brooklyn stores, sold as 'appetite' food. Calcium-plus-protein 'bone' lines and creatine are the fastest-growing supplements after the fracture communication. Value multipacks still anchor low-density zips.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~19% from 2025 and beer ~13%. The losses slowed as AUD fills levelled at ~1.1M. Craft distillers in Kentucky consolidated. Some high-end bars market 'unmedicated hours'. Non-alcoholic drinks are ~5% of volume.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Portion tiers are standard, but a premium 'full plate' segment has opened in Austin and Nashville: set menus that advertise large portions and no small-plate option, with diners finishing the meal as the point. QSR value menus carry lower-income markets, where regain after gray-supply interruptions drives traffic.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Thin-cut 'Ozempic fit' denim is discounted and the cheap look of 2032. Growth is in shoulder-and-thigh tailoring for muscled bodies and in resale for cyclers. Size runs are still set by zip code.

fitness.state: Strength training is the growth line, now pushed by the fracture communication. Medicare Advantage plans added resistance-training benefits, and DXA-plus-coaching memberships run $250–450 a month. Budget chains sell 'bone and grip' add-ons. Longevity clinics in Scottsdale and Miami bundle in-person prescribing, DXA and VO2-max testing to satisfy state rules.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is still 29%. Pharmacy trend is ~+6% as net prices stopped falling. Part D premiums rose again. DXA utilisation is up sharply. Workers' comp carriers have begun asking about incretin use in fall claims at warehouse employers, which sits awkwardly with the same employers' adherence tracks. LSA wellness reimbursement covers ~23% of large employers.

pharma.state: Volume is up ~4% on stable prices. Lilly is supply-constrained on retatrutide 12 mg, and Novo is defending its EPI verdict and oral patents. Litigation and counterfeit-defence spending exceeds $1.5B a year across the four majors. Bimagrumab's sponsor is the window's winner on fracture fear. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness alone no longer signals money; it signals a $25 vial. The body that signals status now is muscled, appetitive and visibly eats: shoulders, grip, a full plate finished in public. The irony is that many of those bodies run on a low-dose 'not for weight' pill, bimagrumab and a coach. Thin, soft and bruised monthly is still the employer-track body. Thin and frail at 70 now reads as a fracture risk, not success.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Austin and Charlotte the boast moved again, from biomarkers to 'unmedicated vitality', claimed by people who often are on a longevity plan they describe as 'just bloodwork'. 'Natty' accusations, borrowed from bodybuilding, are the new gossip. Along the Columbus corridor, the thin track body is standard and slightly déclassé. In Memphis and the Delta, gray 'reta' still delivers surgical-grade losses, and thinness there is defended as an achievement against the people who now sneer at it. Retirees in The Villages talk about DXA T-scores the way they once talked about cholesterol.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Two rituals coexist. Upper-income 'appetite dinners' treat eating heartily as display, while weekday meals in high-density zips stay short and protein-led. Bread Alone claims ~900 congregations. Grandparents deprescribed after fracture advice are told to eat more protein, sometimes by grandchildren on plans.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added an 'unmedicated' self-attested badge in 2036, and about a fifth of users with it are later reported by matches as lying. 'Lean-mass verified' remains a premium tier. 'Reset' badges still read as either reliable or flat. Being seen to eat on a first date has become a signal.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, appetite has been rehabilitated as a sign of vitality, as long as it is displayed rather than suffered, while cravings to bet or buy are still classed as noise. In lower-income communities appetite still means lost access. Unmuted claims the aesthetic inversion as its own. MAHA claims it as a return to real food. Both mostly ignore that the people performing appetite can afford to.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at weight doses vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide. The low-dose population is larger and still unmeasured: ~10M licensed longevity, ~3.6M calm/focus, ~1.3M Reset, plus ~6M gray microdosers. ~7.9M workers are in adherence-verified tracks; LSAs at ~23% of large employers reimburse platform fees.
interior_life.framing: Employers say 'steadiness', and platforms say 'metabolic balance'. Clinicians say dose-related side effect. Unmuted says workplace sedative. The newest framing, from the inversion, is that blunted people are 'flat', and in upper-tier social life flat has become a mild insult even as their employers reward it.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Track enrollees at Columbus-corridor 3PLs and national call-centre operators are still promoted at about twice the rate of non-enrollees. After the fracture communication, two large 3PLs added grip-strength and DXA checks to their monitored tracks, so the worker who is verified as adherent and verified as sturdy is now the preferred profile. In July 2036 the Southern District of Ohio denied the call-centre operator's summary-judgment motion in the promotion case, and trial is set for 2037. Attrition-analytics vendors now sell 'steady and strong' cohorts.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per active account is down ~17% from 2032 in high-density states, though it has plateaued as Reset enrolment fell after ad bans. 'Unmedicated' food and travel creators are the fastest-growing genre, and exposés of creators found on plans have become the next one. Ambient programming for the calm segment continues. Stand-up has moved on from the flat audience to the 'natty' liar.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch remains the top couples' complaint. A new one is partners disagreeing over whether to come off for the sake of 'vitality' when one partner's employer track rewards staying on. Older couples manage a deprescribed spouse's regain and a medicated spouse's fracture risk at once.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The restriction coalition widened. MAHA legislators, progressive consumer advocates and now senior-advocacy groups pushed age bans into five more states and DXA rules into nine. They still never touched adherence premiums: business lobbies held, and Illinois is still alone. Gaming money continues to back limits on Reset advertising. 'Unmedicated' has become a campaign word for some MAHA candidates, a few of whom are on plans.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on approved products, restrictive on youth, older adults' safety, marketing and telehealth. The FDA approved nothing new in class and issued the Jun 2035 fracture Drug Safety Communication. Sixteen states now have under-12 weight-indication bans (Georgia, Alabama, South Carolina, Kentucky and Kansas joined in 2035–36). Ten require an in-person visit for low-BMI adult prescribing, nine require a DXA within 24 months for prescribing to adults 65+, and nine ban social-media advertising of off-label uses. Congress passed nothing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx operates on manufacturer prices, frozen in this window. The Medicare Bridge pilot was not revived. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands. A CMS quality measure on DXA-before-renewal took effect in 2036.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Clinic administration records, PBM fills, telehealth check-ins and LSA claims flow to wellness vendors under consent. DXA and grip-strength results now flow into some employer tracks. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE unchanged; the Army recruit oral pilot continues with added bone-density screening after stress-fracture concerns at basic training. DOT guidance treating prescribed, disclosed incretins as non-disqualifying stands. Gray use remains undisclosed.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's parcel registration (Jan 2035) cut direct Indian mail by roughly a third, and the flow shifted to Chinese API shipped in bulk to domestic fill-and-finish labs in Nevada, Texas and Florida. Import alerts cover more Chinese makers, and Beijing protested again. The US cash-to-generic gap is ~45–70×.

events.event: India's export registration for consumer pharmaceutical parcels takes effect; seizures of Indian semaglutide parcels fall, while CBP and state police report a surge in Chinese bulk peptide powder bound for domestic vial-filling operations

Jury in the first exocrine pancreatic insufficiency bellwether awards a plaintiff $38 million; Novo and Lilly announce no further cash-price reductions in 2035 or 2036, citing litigation reserves and retatrutide supply

FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication after a Medicare analysis links two or more years of incretin use in people over 65 to roughly a one-third higher hip-fracture risk, recommending bone scans before and during treatment for older adults, postmenopausal women and lean users
CDC ties about 240 sepsis and abscess cases and six deaths in 14 states to 'reta' vials from a Nevada repackager selling to longevity and gym customers

Five more states pass under-12 bans, bringing the total to sixteen, as nine states now require a bone scan before prescribing incretins to adults over 65; licensed longevity plans reach ten million subscribers while selling themselves as 'not for weight'
events.driver: state_action: restriction; new_indications: longevity_wellness; cultural_response: aesthetic_inversion

events.event: Ohio federal judge lets a former call-centre agent's promotion-discrimination suit proceed to trial; the same month two national logistics firms add grip-strength and bone-scan checks to their monitored metabolic tracks

open_tensions: Employers reward the adherent and now the sturdy, while their workers' comp carriers start asking whether the drug they reward is breaking warehouse workers' wrists. The Ohio trial in 2037 and the first fracture comp disputes will arrive together, with the 30% premium guidance still standing.

The status body is now 'unmedicated vitality', yet about sixteen million adults without obesity take a low-dose 'not for weight' plan or gray vial, with ~2–3% hip bone loss in two years and an anhedonia rate nobody has measured.

Restriction keeps moving users from licensed channels to a gray market that has relocated from Indian mailers to domestic fill-and-finish labs, out of reach of import alerts. Gray use is now nearly a quarter of all users.

Prices froze on litigation and patents, not policy. A reversal of the EPI verdict on appeal or the tirzepatide non-CVD dementia decision could restart price cuts or harden the freeze, and Medicare is deprescribing frail elders who then regain fat rather than muscle.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: America's new status body lifts, eats a full plate, and keeps its 'not for weight' pill quiet
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036, about eighty million American adults take an incretin drug, a little under three in ten. Two in five have tried one. The total barely moved in two years. The mix changed. Older users came off after the bone scans, and younger, leaner users came on, many of them through the mail.

Prices stopped falling. In April 2035 a jury awarded a woman with a failed pancreas thirty-eight million dollars, an appeals court upheld Novo's pill patents, and both big manufacturers announced that cash prices would hold. They have held. The Wegovy pill is $179 at maintenance and starting pills are still $149. Retatrutide 12 mg costs $299, when a pharmacy has it in stock. The Wegovy box still says $1,349. Employers cover weight drugs at the same 29 percent as before, and Medicare still pays only through heart, kidney, diabetes, sleep and narrow dementia codes. Medicare now wants a bone scan first.

The bone scan is the story of these two years. In June 2035 the FDA told doctors what orthopaedic wards in Florida and Arizona already knew: people over sixty-five who stay on these drugs for years break their hips about a third more often, and more often still if they have cycled on and off. That comes to more than twenty thousand extra hip fractures a year, in a population that once thought the drug was making it younger. Retirees in The Villages compare T-scores. Some came off, regained fat rather than muscle, and are told to eat more protein by grandchildren who are on plans themselves.

The lean young came on anyway. Ten million adults without obesity pay for licensed 'metabolic health' plans, which are now sold as 'not for weight', and about six million more buy vials. That second group grew because states kept adding rules: in-person visits for lean adults, bone scans for the old, and sixteen states with bans for children under twelve. When India began registering pharmaceutical parcels in 2035, the supply did not stop. It moved to Chinese powder filled into vials in Nevada and Texas. One repackager's 'reta' sent about 240 people to hospital with sepsis, and six died. Nearly a quarter of all users are now on product no regulator has seen.

Culture turned on thinness because thinness got cheap. In Austin and Charlotte, a thin body says you found a Telegram seller. A body with shoulders that visibly eats says you have a coach, a scan and time. Restaurants in Nashville sell full plates as a luxury, and butter sells well in Brooklyn. Dating apps offer an 'unmedicated' badge that a fifth of its users are accused of faking. The people performing appetite are often on a low-dose pill and an expensive muscle antibody. Nobody calls that a contradiction out loud.

At work the preference for the steady has gained a second test. Freight hubs on the Columbus corridor still promote monitored-track enrollees at twice the rate of other workers. Two logistics firms now also test grip strength and bone density, so the ideal shift lead is adherent and sturdy. A judge in Ohio has sent the first promotion-discrimination case to trial. Workers' comp adjusters have started asking about incretins in fall claims at the same firms that reward them.

Congress did nothing. Illinois is still the only state that forbids charging workers more for missed doses. Spirits volumes are down nearly a fifth. Sportsbook operators say betting has levelled off. Everything works, and more of it is measured, scanned or monitored than before.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tamika Hale wakes at 4:40 in Groveport and checks the clinic app. Her MariTide shot is due Thursday and her adherence bar is green. The bar keeps her premium thirty percent lower, so she keeps it green.

At the warehouse, the track nurse has a new machine. Squeeze, she says. Tamika squeezes. Thirty-one kilos. Good, the nurse says, and books her DXA for March. Tamika has been a shift lead for two years. Darnell, who quit the track, has not been promoted, and nobody says why.

At lunch she eats half a turkey wrap and gives the rest to a picker named Kyle. Kyle is twenty-three, enormous in the shoulders, and says he has never taken anything. Nobody believes him.

After shift she drives to her mother's. Gloria, seventy-one, wears a wrist brace from the November fall. Her heart doctor took her off Ozempic after the scan. 'I'm hungry all the time,' Gloria says, pleased about it, and makes cornbread. Tamika takes a small square. Her mother watches her not finish it.

Her daughter Aaliyah texts from Columbus State: a picture of a steak dinner with friends, captioned 'we ATE.' The restaurant has no small plates. The price is cut off.

At home Tamika's husband is asleep on the couch with the betting app closed. He has been on a Reset plan for a year, $129 a month, and the LSA pays the platform fee. He is calmer now, and she still can't tell whether he has changed.

She sets the alarm for 4:40. Thursday is three days off.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Novo and Lilly announce no further cash-price reductions in 2035 or 2036, citing litigation reserves and retatrutide supply
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a single $38M bellwether verdict on semaglutide is trivial for two firms with a $150B+ market. It does not explain why Lilly, whose tirzepatide and retatrutide were not at issue, would also freeze prices. The stalled-price driver is stipulated, but this causal story is thin.

least_plausible_claims.quote: nine states now require a bone scan before prescribing incretins to adults over 65
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: nine state laws are enacted and in force within about nine months of the June 2035 FDA communication. The FDA warning only moved the hip-fracture HR from ~1.3 to ~1.35, after a class bone warning already existed since 2028. The speed and the weak trigger are asserted, not shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: bimagrumab demand up sharply after the fracture communication but still almost no cash channel
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: bimagrumab is a lean-mass adjunct priced at $1,150 list, with no bone indication yet.
